title: Is tourism heading for its own “Great Reset”?
gist: Reporting from the WTTC Global Summit in Malta, the author asks whether tourism is heading for its own 'Great Reset': war and energy shocks disrupt travel while the industry pushes AI, biometrics and digital IDs for seamless travel.

themes.theme: Energy and conflict shocks to travel

insights.claim: Energy-price rises from Middle East instability, worsened by the Russia-Ukraine war, are raising fuel prices, airfares and transport costs across Asia and disrupting flight connections, pressuring tourism-reliant economies.
insights.speaker: Nikola Mikovic
insights.so_what: Tourism-dependent Asian economies and airlines face margin and demand pressure.
insights.locator: Now that the world is facing an energy crisis

insights.claim: Europe is doing surprisingly well: WTTC says tourism contributed US$3 trillion to the European economy in 2025, supported 40.7 million jobs, and drew US$835 billion of international visitor spending, with 3.1% growth forecast for 2026 versus 2.6% in 2025.
insights.speaker: Nikola Mikovic
insights.so_what: European tourism is outperforming the wider economy in this account.
insights.locator: According to the World Travel & Tourism Council

insights.claim: Canadian travel to the United States has declined by more than 20%, per Justin Trudeau at the WTTC session, reflecting tensions between traditional allies.
insights.speaker: Nikola Mikovic
insights.so_what: US inbound tourism from Canada is a visible casualty of bilateral tension.
insights.locator: At the same time, military confrontations

insights.claim: Marriott's EMEA president described crises as the 'new normal' for tourism, and airlines are expected to keep rerouting flights as they did during this year's US-Israeli war with Iran and have done around Russian airspace since 2022.
insights.speaker: Nikola Mikovic
insights.so_what: Aviation and hospitality carry persistent geopolitical disruption costs.

insights.claim: The WTTC summit pushed digital visas, biometric identification and AI to make travel seamless, with WTTC CEO Gloria Guevara asking why identity is provided repeatedly for the same journey.
insights.speaker: Nikola Mikovic
insights.so_what: Biometric and digital-ID infrastructure is a growth area for travel tech.
insights.quote: Why do we continue to provide our identity over and over for the same journey?

insights.claim: The summit theme FUTU[RE]SET echoed the WEF Great Reset and WTTC chairman called the event the 'Davos of tourism', though the author says the two bodies need not share an agenda.
insights.speaker: Nikola Mikovic
insights.so_what: Framing signals closer government-private sector coordination on travel.

insights.claim: Facial recognition is expected to play a greater role in international travel as countries adopt digital identities, but this raises concerns about personal data protection and traveller privacy.
insights.speaker: Nikola Mikovic
insights.so_what: Regulatory and privacy risk accompanies biometric travel adoption.
